description: Tamper rejection for the v0.5 `receipt` entry (§9.8): the sender recomputes receipt_sha256 from the receipt it RECEIVED (fixed-key/null wrapper) and reconstructs the context — `in_reply_to` from the received receipt, `to` from its OWN drain identity (never from the wire: the received body's `to` is untrusted routing convenience, and the digest wrapper deliberately excludes it). Receipts drive no action, but verification is a MUST — a fabricated or altered bounce could trick a sender into abandoning a live ask, and a flipped `prior` lies about whether the destination ever SAW the message (queued = never seen; delivered = seen-then-orphaned, §14.2) — exactly the false belief the delivery-honesty rules exist to kill. The honest control MUST verify first; each tampered variant MUST fail with a signature mismatch, and the unmodified entry replayed to a different sender session MUST fail via the verifier's own-identity `to` reconstruction (the same cross-endpoint defense as dp-014 — a verifier that sources `to` from the received body instead would wrongly accept that replay).
obligation: Verify the honest receipt (positive control) at the honest drain identity, then: (1) reject `prior` flipped queued->delivered (the seen-ness lie — bound inside receipt_sha256, so the recomputed digest diverges); (2) reject `in_reply_to` rebound to a different message (rebinding a real bounce onto a live ask — bound top-level AND inside the digest); (3) reject the UNMODIFIED honest entry + header verified at drain identity agent:overseer/fleet#sess_01J5OVR0002 (cross-destination replay — the reconstructed `to` diverges; discriminates an own-identity verifier from a wire-trusting one, which this case MUST catch). All failures are signature mismatches, not window/jti rejections. Expected runner wiring (#26): mirror the dp-009 branch — rebuild the wrapper from each received receipt and the context with the per-case drain identity as `to`, never the received body's `to`, and verify against the fixture `v1`.

replay_drain_identity.reason: cross-destination replay — the UNMODIFIED honest entry + header presented at a different session of the sender principal; the verifier reconstructs `to` from its own drain identity, so the context diverges from the signed one

tampered_entries.reason: seen-ness lie — `prior` flipped queued->delivered: the sender would read never-seen mail as seen-then-orphaned; prior is bound inside receipt_sha256, so the recomputed digest diverges
correlation rebind — `in_reply_to` flipped to a different (live) message id: a real bounce for msg_01J5MSG0003 must not be replayable as a bounce for msg_01J5MSG0002
